annotationRationale: Spatial coordinates convert the geographic data into a chord length, and the cosine law recovers the central angle. Pythagoras supports the coordinate calculations, while special-angle cosine values identify 120 degrees.
sourceMethod: Follows the official coordinate, chord-distance, and law-of-cosines solution. Names the equatorial projection H to explain the coordinate relations that the official text states directly.

review.mathCheck: The eastward longitude difference is 135 degrees. On the unit sphere, latitude 45 degrees gives \(B=(-1/2,1/2,\sqrt{2}/2)\) relative to \(A=(1,0,0)\). Therefore \(AB^2=3\), and the cosine law gives \(\cos\angle ACB=-1/2\). The angle is 120 degrees, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Q23, pages 14-15, using coordinates, chord length and the cosine law. Its coordinate signs agree with the official sphere figure. The added projection H explains the construction without requiring that figure.
review.annotationCheck: The geographic interpretation, projection, positive coordinate parameter and central-angle recovery are fully explained. The selected method requires no dot-product knowledge.
